# auth_base.html: missing |escapejs on auth_url/register_url/passkey_url turns & into &amp; — group-scoped portals silently lose the redirect param

- **Kind**: bug — **Priority**: should — **Project**: django-mojo
- **Board**: https://maestromojo.com/workspaces/#/board/11?item=1092

## Description

`mojo/apps/account/templates/account/auth_base.html` interpolates several server-built URLs into JS string literals with **no `|escapejs`**:

```js
var AUTH_URL = "{{ auth_url|default:'/auth' }}";
var REGISTER_URL = "{{ register_url|default:'/register' }}";
var PASSKEY_URL = "{{ passkey_url|default:'/passkey' }}";
```

Those values are built in `mojo/apps/account/rest/bouncer/views.py` as `f'/{path}{group_qs}'`, where `group_qs` is `'?' + urlencode(fwd_params)` and `fwd_params` carries `group_uuid` **plus** the forwarded `redirect` / `next` / `returnTo` / `back` values.

With two or more params the query string contains `&`. Django's autoescaping rewrites it to `&amp;`, and **the HTML parser does not decode entities inside `<script>`**, so the JS string literal ends up holding a literal `&amp;`. `register.html` then assigns `cfg.passkeyUrl` straight to `window.location.href`, and the destination receives `?group_uuid=…&amp;redirect=…` — so the redirect parameter is parsed as `amp;redirect` and **silently dropped** for every group-scoped portal.

This is not a new class of bug in this file: `tests/test_auth/bouncer_forms.py` already pins exactly this for `bouncer_challenge.html`, which **does** use `|escapejs`. These three siblings never got it.

## Not an XSS

Autoescaping still neutralizes `<` and `"`, so there is no string or tag breakout — this is a **correctness** bug, not an injection one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `auth_url`, `register_url` and `passkey_url` carry `|escapejs`
- [ ] A group-scoped portal that forwards a `redirect` param navigates to a URL where that param is intact and parseable — regression test failing on the current template
- [ ] Audit the rest of the file for the same omission rather than fixing only these three
- [ ] Single-param URLs (the common case, `?group_uuid=` alone) behave exactly as today

## Out of scope

- `#1068`'s scheme guard (done)
- Restructuring how `bouncer/views.py` builds the forwarded query string

---

## Plan

**Build order: FOURTH / last in this batch.** Fully independent — no file overlap with #1088/#1089/#1091 except `CHANGELOG.md` (append to `## Unreleased`, do not disturb existing entries).

### Objective

Give every `{{ … }}` that lands inside a JS string literal in `auth_base.html` the `|escapejs` filter, so a server-built URL carrying two or more query params reaches the browser intact instead of with `&` rewritten to `&amp;`. Pin it with a regression test, and leave the file with zero unescaped JS-string interpolations.

**Verified mechanism (re-derived end to end):** `_auth_context` builds `fwd_params` = `group_uuid` plus any of `redirect`/`next`/`returnTo`/`back`, then `group_qs = f'?{urlencode(fwd_params)}'`; the three URLs are `f'/{path}{group_qs}'`; the template interpolates them into JS string literals with no `|escapejs`; autoescape rewrites `&`→`&amp;` and `<script>` is a raw-text element so the parser never decodes it back; `register.html` assigns `cfg.passkeyUrl` to `window.location.href`; the destination parses `amp;redirect` and drops `redirect`. Django's `escapejs` maps `&`→`&`, `=`→`=`, `-`→`-`, quotes/`<`/`>`/`;`/backtick/controls, and returns a `SafeString` so autoescape does not re-run.

### Steps

1. **Fix the five JS-string interpolations** in `auth_base.html`, appending `|escapejs` **after** the `default:` filter (matching the in-file precedent on the `passkey_prompt` / `group_uuid` neighbours and the cross-file precedent in `bouncer_challenge.html`): `api_base`, `success_redirect`, `auth_url`, `register_url`, `passkey_url`. Add a short comment stating the rule — see **m2** for the required comment syntax.
2. **Do not touch** the `href` occurrences of the same values in `login.html`, `register.html`, `passkey_enroll.html` and `auth_base.html`. Attributes *are* entity-decoded by the HTML parser, so those links already work today; adding `escapejs` there would inject a literal `=` and break them.
3. **Add the regression tests** to `tests/test_auth/bouncer_forms.py` — see **M1**/**M2** for placement and shape.
4. **CHANGELOG entry** — see **M5** for the wording constraint.
5. Builder runs `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_auth.bouncer_forms` for the targeted check; the batch's closing full sweep is the verification of record.

### Design decisions

- **`|escapejs`, not `|safe`, not a server-side change.** `|safe` would fix the ampersand but reopen the string-literal breakout that autoescape currently closes. Changing how `views.py` builds `group_qs` is explicitly out of scope and is the wrong layer — the value is correct; only its transport into a JS literal is wrong. `escapejs` is already the in-tree answer to exactly this bug.
- **Fix all five JS literals, not only the three named.** `ON_SUCCESS` is a live instance of the same bug: `theme.success_redirect` is tenant-writable, unvalidated, flows to the navigation sink, and a value with two query params is corrupted today. `API_BASE` cannot realistically carry `&`, but leaving one unescaped literal preserves the pattern that produced this bug twice; the runtime string is provably unchanged, so the cost is zero.
- **Leave the `yesno` boolean alone** — it renders a bare (unquoted) JS boolean from a two-value vocabulary, so it is not a string literal and `escapejs` there would be meaningless. Recorded so a future sweep does not "complete" it.
- **Leave `custom_css|safe` alone** — `<style>` is raw text, so `|safe` is *required* for the CSS to work at all. Different context, different class. (See **m4** for the precise scope of its validation gate.)
- **Assertions decode the JS escapes before parsing** rather than string-matching the rendered HTML. After the fix the raw HTML changes even for a single-param URL (`?group_uuid=…`) though the runtime string does not, so a `contains` assertion would be brittle and would not prove the acceptance criterion. Decoding `\uXXXX` then `parse_qs` reproduces exactly what the browser does.
- **Stay with `escapejs` rather than restructuring the whole `_matConfig` through `json_script`.** That would retire this bug class permanently, but minimal-diff-for-a-bug and consistency with the three existing `escapejs` sites win. Recorded so the next reader does not relitigate it.
- **No docs edit.** `docs/web_developer/account/bouncer.md` already documents forwarded params as preserved in navigation links; the fix makes the docs true. Editing them would mean documenting the bug. The escaping contract goes in the template comment, where the next person adding a context var will see it.

### Amendments from the challenge round (BINDING)

**M1 — reuse the existing helper; do not append at the cited line.** `tests/test_auth/bouncer_forms.py` is **763 lines**, and `_render_switcher` (~line 648) already *is* the proposed helper: RequestFactory + `request.DATA = objict.objict(...)` + `_auth_context` + `render()`, returning `(html, ctx)`. It sits under a "Switcher param forwarding" section whose tests cover this precise feature. Meanwhile line 616 is **inside the f-string assertion message of an existing test** — appending there would split it. → Reuse `_render_switcher`; append new tests at EOF under their own banner.

**M2 — the primary regression test would otherwise pass on the broken template (critical).** `_auth_context` derives the group from the **kwarg only** (`group_uuid = group.uuid if group else ''`); it never reads `group_uuid` out of `request.DATA`, whose forwarding loop whitelists only `redirect`/`next`/`returnTo`/`back`. So supplying `group_uuid` as a query param with `group=None` yields a single `fwd_param`, no `&`, no `&amp;` — **green against the broken template**, violating the acceptance criterion and the repo's "regressions must fail while broken" rule. → Pass `group=opts.group` (mirroring the existing test in that section) **and** add a precondition assertion that `ctx['register_url']` contains a literal `&` before asserting on the rendered literal.

**M3 — keep escapejs-after-default, drop the false rationale.** All four hosted pages route through `_auth_context`, which unconditionally sets these keys, so rendering with `group=None` yields `/auth` *from the context*, not from `default:` — the proposed assertion cannot distinguish filter orders. The order is also functionally inert (`escapejs` returns a `SafeString` that `default` passes through). Keep the order (still correct for a downstream template overrider rendering without these keys) but do not claim the test pins it; if pinning is wanted, `ctx.pop('auth_url')` before rendering.

**M4 — the audit test's script slice must be anchored.** Two `<script>` tags open consecutively: an **external** one whose `src="{{ api_base }}…"` is a double-quoted interpolation that must **NOT** be escapejs'd, and then the inline block. A naive slice from the first `<script` would capture the external tag and fail the audit on a correct line. → Anchor on the inline opener (the `<script nonce=…>` with no `src=`) through its matching `</script>`. Also state in the docstring that this is a double-quoted-only guard, so it is not mistaken for complete coverage (it structurally cannot see unquoted or single-quoted interpolations).

**M5 — the CHANGELOG must not overstate the blast radius.** `cfg.authUrl` and `cfg.registerUrl` are published on `_matConfig` but read by **nothing** in the tree; the login↔register switcher navigates via `href`, which is entity-decoded and therefore **not broken today**. The one live user-visible break is the register→passkey-enrollment hop, plus `ON_SUCCESS` when a tenant configures a multi-param `success_redirect`. → Word the entry around those two, and add one line noting the runtime value of `_matConfig.*Url` changes for out-of-tree consumers (`&amp;` → `&`).

**m2 — comment syntax.** The rule comment must be `{% comment %}`, a **single-line** `{# #}`, or a JS `//`. A multi-line `{# … #}` renders as literal page text and trips the existing test that greps rendered output of all four hosted templates for `{#`/`{{`/`{%`.

**m3 — `_decode_js` must handle the full escape set** (`-`, `=`, `;`, backtick, `<`, `>`, quotes), not just `&`. Use a `\\u([0-9a-fA-F]{4})` regex sub — a blanket `unicode_escape` decode mangles non-ASCII. Note the module's group fixture uses a deliberately hyphen-free uuid for this reason.

**m4 — don't overstate the `custom_css` gate** in the new comment: `validate_custom_css` runs on the REST write path only; the settings and test-header paths reach `theme.custom_css` without it. Operator/test-mode trust boundaries, not a live hole, and out of scope here — just don't write the claim as unconditional.

**Rebutted:** the line-number nit on the cited sibling test (immaterial — the builder re-derives), and the suggestion to switch to `json_script` (see Design decisions).

### Edge cases

- **Single-param (`?group_uuid=` alone) — the common case.** Runtime string byte-identical; only the HTML source changes (`=` → `=`). Verified no existing test greps the raw `var AUTH_URL/REGISTER_URL/PASSKEY_URL/API_BASE/ON_SUCCESS` lines. Pinned by a dedicated test anyway.
- **No group, no forwarded params.** `escapejs('/auth') == '/auth'` — no-op.
- **Hyphens** → `-` in source; forwarded `redirect` values routinely contain them, another reason assertions decode rather than string-match.
- **Double escaping** — impossible; `escapejs` returns a `SafeString`.
- **CSP** — nonce-based, not hash-based, so changing inline script bytes cannot invalidate the policy.
- **`contact.html`** extends `auth_base.html` and inherits the fix with no separate change; same for `login.html`, `register.html`, `passkey_enroll.html`.
- **Interaction with #1068** — the scheme guard still governs whether navigation happens; this fix only restores the query string. It cannot weaken the guard.

### Testing plan

All in `tests/test_auth/bouncer_forms.py`, appended at EOF under a new banner, reusing `_render_switcher` plus a small `_js_literal(html, var_name)` and `_decode_js(s)` helper:

1. `test_auth_base_forwarded_urls_survive_autoescape` — render with `group=opts.group` and a `redirect` param. Precondition: `ctx['register_url']` contains `&`. Then for `AUTH_URL`/`REGISTER_URL`/`PASSKEY_URL`: no `&amp;` in the literal; decoded literal parses with `redirect` present and correct, `group_uuid` present, and **no** `amp;redirect` key. **Fails on the current template.**
2. `test_auth_base_success_redirect_survives_autoescape` — group metadata `theme.success_redirect` with two params (try/finally restore, the pattern already used in this file); decoded `ON_SUCCESS` parses both params with no `amp;` key. **Fails today.**
3. `test_auth_base_single_param_urls_unchanged` — group-only render: each decoded literal exactly `/auth?group_uuid=<uuid>` etc., no `&` present. Proves the common case is untouched.
4. `test_auth_base_script_literals_all_escapejs` — read the raw template off disk (idiom already used in `tests/test_auth/handoff.py`), slice the **inline** script block per M4, regex every double-quoted `{{ }}`, assert each contains `escapejs`. Failure message names the offending interpolation. Standing form of the audit criterion.

Not tested, deliberately: the `window.location.href` assignment executing — there is no JS runtime in the suite, and an existing test already pins that the sink exists.

### Schema impact

None.

### Contract changes

- No endpoint, signature or serialization change. `_auth_context` returns the same values; only their rendering into the page changes.
- **Runtime behavior change (the fix):** `_matConfig.authUrl`/`registerUrl`/`passkeyUrl` and the post-auth `redirectTo` now hold the real URL when it carries two or more query params. The visible consequence is that a group-scoped portal forwarding `?redirect=` lands the visitor at that destination after the passkey hop instead of at the group's `success_redirect` / `/`.
- **One observable wrinkle:** the rendered HTML source now contains `=` / `&` / `-` inside those five literals. Anything scraping the page source with a naive regex must decode the JS escapes first. No in-tree consumer does.
- **Unchanged:** the switcher `<a href>` links — attribute context, already correct, deliberately not modified.

### Full-file audit (all 24 interpolations)

- **Missing `|escapejs` → fix**: `api_base`, `success_redirect`, `auth_url`, `register_url`, `passkey_url` (the five JS string literals).
- **Already correct**: `passkey_prompt`, `group_uuid` (both already carry `|escapejs`).
- **Correct by construction, leave alone**: `login_methods|json_script` (safe idiom); `skip_session_check|yesno` (unquoted boolean, fixed vocabulary); `custom_css|safe` (required for `<style>`).
- **Attribute/text contexts, autoescape is correct**: `page_title` (×2), `favicon_url`, `api_base` (×2 in attributes), `custom_css_url`, `logo_url`, `brand_name` (×2), `csp_nonce` (×2).

**Noted for the orchestrator, not planned here:** `contact.html` has two interpolations in the same shape and `bouncer_decoy.html` interpolates a colour into a `<style>` block — all three inert today (hard-coded or validated values), so there is no bug to fix, only a pattern. Not in this item's file scope.
